races.name: Betway Leigh Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's mount is the form pick here — back-to-back wins on good ground over 10f and now stepping up to 12f, which looks a natural trip extension; a genuine hold-up horse who needs Relentless Hero to post a genuine gallop, and Murphy's big-race tactical awareness gives him an edge.
runners_data.comment: Brighton View arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the chief concern is whether six days is enough recovery time at 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Mandarin Spirit
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott takes over on this Kevin Ryan three-year-old who won over 7f on good ground but has been beaten at 10f subsequently; the step to 12f is a notable query for a horse whose form trail suggests he may be more speed than stamina, though good ground ticks the box.
runners_data.comment: Mandarin Spirit showed she retains the ability to win when scoring a winner five starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going, she appeals as the one to beat here despite a dip in form since — carrying 135 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero
runners_data.note: Colin Keane on the Andrew Balding-trained sole front-runner — 42 days off the track is worth noting, but Balding's operation has a solid 14-day strike rate and Keane winning abroad recently keeps confidence high; the lone lead is a massive tactical asset on this flat, galloping track.
runners_data.comment: Relentless Hero won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, arriving here on a sound enough platform from stall three carrying 132 lb — the main concern is that eighth last time out, which demands explanation before confidence builds.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has solid placed form on good ground and Daniel Tudhope is a shrewd judge of pace, but this horse's natural style is to come from off the pace — held up in rear — and with other true closers filling the same space, he cannot get the clean run he needs to produce his best.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and fresh on 16 days' rest, Saxophonist arrives with experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 76 offers encouragement — third three starts back and again four starts back underlines his knack for filling the frame, though he remains winless in recent starts and must convert that placed consistency into a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Claytons Kolatonic
runners_data.note: Dominic Ffrench Davis's lightly-framed three-year-old has the lowest OR in the field (59) and a single run on good ground from five starts, which is a concern on today's surface; held up naturally, he has been repositioned to midfield on the map simply because the true rear is crowded, and his chance looks slim at this level.

runners_data.name: Lc Tiffen
runners_data.note: Lisa Williamson's mare runs just 12 days after her last start (3rd over 10f on good ground, which is her best effort) and has placed credentials at this trip; Molly Gunn's 5lb claim helps with the weight, but as a natural hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role, she faces the same crowding problem as the other redistributed closers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a ninth and an unplaced run among recent efforts making her hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, though she does return on a quick turnaround having run over today's distance and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Relentless Hero is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no genuine rivals for the lead, Colin Keane can dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front. The pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching — sustainable enough to avoid blowing up, but also potentially slow enough in the middle sectionals to make it extremely difficult for hold-up horses to reel him in. Brighton View and Mandarin Spirit are the genuine closers who must rely on Relentless Hero setting enough tempo to create a true test of stamina. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Saxophonist, Claytons Kolatonic, and Lc Tiffen are all true hold-up horses compressed into the midfield by redistribution, meaning none of them will get their preferred patient position cleanly, and their effectiveness is diluted as a result. This race shape strongly favours the lone front-runner and any prominent racer capable of tracking him, as the absence of pace pressure means the lead is unlikely to be surrendered freely in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Relentless Hero Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Relentless Hero leads at a comfortable clip and no rival has the pace or inclination to pressurise him through the middle mile.
scenarios.body: Keane settles Relentless Hero in front on a soft lead, controls the tempo through the long Haydock straight, and kicks clear before the closers can organise a challenge; his Good-ground form (0W0P but placed at this trip) suits the conditions and the lack of an honest pace makes the front the place to be.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Relentless Hero sets a strong enough tempo — faster than expected — that opens the race up for a late finisher with a strong finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Brighton View, the most progressive three-year-old in the field (two wins recently, good going OK, Oisin Murphy aboard), is best-placed to capitalise with a powerful late run from off the pace; Mandarin Spirit, winner on good ground over 7f, would also be in the mix if the pace genuinely collapsed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Tracks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a rival manages to sit just behind Relentless Hero at a respectful distance and outstays him in the final furlong as he weakens.
scenarios.body: With the true hold-up horses displaced from their natural rear positions, any runner who can comfortably track the leader in second or third carries a positional edge into the straight; Saxophonist, despite being redistributed, has the form figures to be dangerous if he can navigate a forward spot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Relentless Hero is headed or slows dramatically in the straight, triggering a chaotic finish from a bunched midfield group.
scenarios.body: Claytons Kolatonic and Lc Tiffen are both out of role and at significant style-fit disadvantages, making this the least likely shape; even if the pace collapses, neither has the form or class to dominate a sprint finish at these ratings.

watchPoints.text: Watch Relentless Hero's early sectionals — if Keane finds himself in front unchallenged within the first two furlongs, the race may effectively be over, as no horse in this field has the pace profile or position to burn him off the front.

Brighton View is the chief danger but depends entirely on tempo — if Relentless Hero dictates a slow-medium pace through the middle mile, Murphy may find he has too much ground to make up in the short Haydock straight.

Saxophonist, Claytons Kolatonic, and Lc Tiffen are all competing for the same rear/midfield ground — watch for traffic issues turning for home if they concertina together, reducing the chance of a clean finishing run for any of them.
Mandarin Spirit's stamina for 12f is unproven — Kevin Stott may be forced to commit earlier than ideal if he senses the pace is insufficient, turning a hold-up type into an accidental front-chaser.

Relentless Hero returns after 42 days off; Andrew Balding's horses often need at least one run back, and if he is less than fully wound up, the final 2f could see him stop sharply — the one scenario that would open the race to the closers.

races.name: Betway Rose Of Lancaster Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Convergent
runners_data.note: Has strong credentials at 1m2f on Good ground (1W at this trip/going combination), sits naturally just behind the leader, and Clifford Lee for K. R. Burke is a solid booking; a 30-day break is not a concern and his recent OR-117 marks him as the highest-rated non-Sallaal runner — well-placed to capitalise if Sallaal weakens.
runners_data.comment: Convergent won three starts back and arrives fit on 30 days' rest, bringing distance-and-going experience and a solid rating of 120 to support his claims; the worry is that he has been fourth last time out, so his very best form needs to resurface here.

runners_data.name: Danger Bay
runners_data.note: Boosted by strong recent form including two wins at 1m-1m1f on Good, but his natural front-running tendency is the critical caveat — with Sallaal monopolising the lead, he will need to restrain himself in a midfield berth that does not suit, and his best form has come over shorter than today's 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Nahraan
runners_data.note: Trained by John & Thady Gosden with Oisin Murphy aboard — a premium jockey booking — and his three wins from five starts show ability, but 53 days off and a form line that includes a disappointing 9th last time out on Good ground tempers expectations; he is a naturally prominent horse shown at the rear only because the field's pace commitments leave no room further forward, so Murphy will need to manage his energy carefully.
runners_data.comment: Nahraan won three of his last five starts and was third two runs back, bringing solid recent form to this assignment; he has experience of today's trip and going, and his ranking here underlines his claims — though that ninth last time out is the one blemish to watch.

runners_data.name: Sallaal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's confirmed pace-setter has won his last two outings including a course win at 1m2f on Good, and as the sole front-runner in a field of five on a flat track he gets an uncontested lead — the key tactical advantage in this race shape; his headgear (h) suggests he needs to be kept focused, and the style-fit flag reflects that his role as lone leader in this field is a slight deviation from his usual contested-pace environment.
runners_data.comment: Sallaal arrives in cracking form, a winner last time out and again two starts back, and he has run over today's distance and going before. Carrying 133 lb is the one weight to respect, but on his recent record he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sea Scout
runners_data.note: Returning from a 287-day absence for Simon & Ed Crisford, which is a major concern regardless of ability, and his recent form string of 3-3-4-6-11 over 1m2f-1m3f suggests he is not a horse who wins off the front of a strong gallop — naturally a prominent type who is mapped to midfield here because there is simply no room for him nearer the pace, compounding the fitness question.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in his last two outings with back-to-back thirds, Sea Scout has run over today's trip and going and shaped with promise; the main concern is a lengthy 287-day absence, and he remains winless in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Sallaal is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of only five, he is highly likely to secure an uncontested lead and dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good ground at Haydock. Convergent is the most natural prominent type to sit just behind, with Danger Bay and Sea Scout both true prominent runners who are effectively squeezed into midfield positions they do not naturally occupy, given the surfeit of pace-committed horses relative to the spaces available. Nahraan, a genuine prominent type pushed to the rear by the redistribution logic, is equally unlikely to find himself in his favoured position without expending energy to secure it. The race will be run at a measured, honest pace set by Sallaal, with the first two furlongs shaping the order decisively; given the lack of a genuine hold-up horse to pounce late and the controlled fractions Sallaal is likely to dictate, this race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile — a horse that can travel close to the pace and quicken from the front or just off it — rather than any late-running closer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sallaal Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sallaal gets a clean break and dictates an uncontested, measured pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Sallaal sets fractions to suit himself and quickens entering the straight, making it a true test of quality rather than stamina or finishing speed; horses who travel prominently without burning energy to get position are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent rival — most likely Convergent — tracks Sallaal closely and overpowers him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Convergent's Group-level form at 1m2f on Good ground gives him the profile to sit just off a slow-to-honest pace and produce a decisive finishing effort; K. R. Burke's 14-day strike rate of 7/43 reflects steady but not spectacular current form, yet Clifford Lee will be alive to any opportunity to dictate the race from behind the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Sallaal is pressured early by one of the redistributed prominent types and the pace becomes too hot, setting up a late run.
scenarios.body: Danger Bay or Sea Scout, racing out of their natural positions, might push forward and create a faster-than-expected early gallop that sees the field string out; in that scenario a horse that conserves energy — most plausibly Nahraan, despite being a true prominent type pushed to the rear — could benefit, though this is a low-probability shape because none of the redistribution horses are genuine hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Midfield Shuffle
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners attempt to establish a forward position simultaneously, causing scrimmaging and uneven fractions.
scenarios.body: Sea Scout's lengthy 287-day absence and Danger Bay's tendency to race prominently could combine to disrupt the expected running order in the early stages; this creates an unpredictable race shape that most likely suits whichever horse settles quickest, but given none of the field are true hold-up horses, the disruption is unlikely to produce a dramatic late winner.

watchPoints.text: Sallaal's early jumping and whether any of Danger Bay or Sea Scout attempt to chase him forward — if the opening two furlongs are contested rather than solo, Sallaal's advantage evaporates and the race shape changes fundamentally.

Sea Scout's fitness after 287 days off is the single biggest unknown in the field; watch how he moves to post and whether James Doyle restrains him or allows him to stride on early, as either choice carries risk.

Nahraan's market moves — if Oisin Murphy's booking attracts strong support for the Gosden yard, it may signal stable confidence that the 53-day break has left him cherry-ripe, elevating his probability above what the pace map suggests.

Convergent's position in the early stages is a key shape indicator; if Clifford Lee pushes to sit directly on Sallaal's heels from the outset, it signals an intent to make this a true test of stamina rather than a solo front-running exercise, and that changes how the straight unfolds.
The Good ground is confirmed consistent across all races on the card, so no late going drift should alter pre-race pace assumptions — take the projected race shape at face value.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Dick Hern Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Alobayyah
runners_data.note: Course-and-distance winner for Haggas and Marquand, with two wins from five runs on Good ground; 52 days off is a routine freshen-up for this stable and she has strong prominent credentials right behind Silenciosa, making her a natural dangers if the race sets up steadily.
runners_data.comment: Alobayyah won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a serious danger from stall four carrying 130 lb; the main concern is a 52-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Aviatrice
runners_data.note: Marnane's filly has done her best work when racing prominently, but in a field saturated with similar types she will likely find herself shuffled further back than she wants; her Good-ground record is mixed (9 places from 15 runs, no wins) and a compromised position will blunt her chance meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Aviatrice arrives on the back of a second last time out and a third two starts back, showing consistent placed form in recent starts, though she was unplaced three starts back; the experience over today's trip and going helps, but 130 lb from stall 1 is the challenge.

runners_data.name: Fallen Angel
runners_data.note: Burke's five-year-old is the class act on paper with an OR of 116 and seven wins from 13 runs on Good ground; fitted with a hood, she arrives 86 days fresh and has won three of her last five starts at this trip and going — tracking Silenciosa from a prominent pitch is exactly what she does best.
runners_data.comment: Fallen Angel has won three of her last five starts, including back-to-back victories three and four starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 130 lb from stall 3, the 86-day absence is the one query, but her rating underlines she is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Maeva
runners_data.note: Fellowes' filly is a hold-up specialist with two wins in the past year, but both came on Soft-to-Standard surfaces and her sole Good-ground run produced a modest fifth; 113 days off is a significant fitness query, and she needs a pace she is unlikely to get in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and below her official mark, Maeva has been out of the form book in her last two starts — fifth and sixth — and returns after a 113-day absence; she has run over today's trip and going, and two wins in her last five starts offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Keatley's consistent mare ran third and fourth in her last two outings on Good ground and has scope to finish well from the rear; only 13 days since her last run suggests she is in a good rhythm, though the modest pace will limit how much ground she can make up late.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Mostar Dreams faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a third last time out and has distance and going experience to call on; 130 lb from stall 11 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Noche Clasica
runners_data.note: Dual course winner for Bethell and Tudhope, both on Good or Soft, and rated OR 98; she won over 9f on Good last time out at a relevant level and is one of the more credible closers if the gallop quickens — her most recent Haydock run (15th) is best overlooked as an anomaly.
runners_data.comment: Noche Clasica won two of her last five starts but has been unplaced last time out and returns after 52 days off; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, yet carrying 130 lb from stall 9 leaves her with plenty to find against a strong field.

runners_data.name: Rumba Numba
runners_data.note: Varian's filly won on Good ground over course and distance most recently and has genuine prominent instincts, but the crowded pace map means she is unlikely to be as close to the front as she ideally needs; the style-fit compromise (0.91) is a real concern, though her raw form is solid.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures and her speed rating of 83 gives little encouragement, but Rumba Numba arrives fit on 11 days' rest, has experience of today's trip and going, and her trainer is firing at 34% — two wins in her last five starts add some substance.

runners_data.name: Blingy's Sister
runners_data.note: Palmer sends a three-year-old with back-to-back placed runs on Good ground, but she is a natural front-to-prominent racer who will find her position squeezed in this field; Murphy is a positive booking, yet racing out of her preferred role (style-fit 0.92) dilutes the chance considerably.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but consistently competitive, Blingy's Sister brings distance and going experience to this contest and was third two starts back and runner-up last time out — the upward trajectory is clear, though she's yet to translate that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Calendar Girl
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three on Good ground and stepping up to a mile for the first time, Burrows' filly has been off 302 days which is the single biggest question mark in the field; if she returns to her best she has the profile to race prominently and quicken, but a 10-month absence from a lightly-raced three-year-old demands caution.
runners_data.comment: Calendar Girl arrives on the back of three wins in her last four starts, including back-to-back victories most recently, and has experience of today's distance and going — but connections must hope 302 days off the track hasn't blunted her edge.

runners_data.name: Pacific Mission
runners_data.note: Balding and Keane team up with an OR-107 filly who has placed in all five career starts on turf but is winless on Good ground (0 from 6, though two seconds); she is a natural prominent type with high-class form and the mile trip suits, though her inability to convert when it matters is a recurring theme.
runners_data.comment: Pacific Mission boasts a solid recent profile — third last time out, a second three starts back, and a winner five starts back — and she has experience of today's trip and conditions. The concern is a 63-day absence heading into this.

runners_data.name: Silenciosa
runners_data.note: The only true front-runner in the race, Clover's three-year-old won on Good ground over 7f and will set the sole pace here; her recent form (6th, 2nd) suggests she is vulnerable once the race quickens, and leading in a Listed race without any pressure may eventually expose her class ceiling in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a winner four starts back, Silenciosa has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid platform, though a midfield ranking and an unplaced effort two starts back suggest she'll need to find improvement to get involved.

races.paceDynamic: Silenciosa is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse prepared to lead, she will set a controlled, solo gallop from the front with no rival willing or able to press her — on Good ground over a mile at Haydock, that is a recipe for a genuine but unhurried pace that keeps the race together until the straight. The cluster of true prominent types — Fallen Angel, Alobayyah, Calendar Girl, and Pacific Mission — will jostle for the positions directly behind Silenciosa, while Blingy's Sister, Rumba Numba, and Aviatrice, all natural front-to-prominent racers, are squeezed into a midfield role they do not naturally want and cannot all escape. Hold-up horses Noche Clasica, Maeva, and Mostar Dreams will be anchored at the rear, needing either a strong enough pace to close into or a well-timed move around the final bend. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner, a compressed mid-pack, and several prominent types racing out of their preferred position — strongly favours horses with a proven prominent profile who can track Silenciosa at will and quicken from a handy position, particularly those with top-class form on Good ground at the trip. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; of the redistributed trio, Fallen Angel and Calendar Girl are the most likely to actually push forward and claim a genuine prominent berth, while Blingy's Sister, Rumba Numba, and Aviatrice face a genuine positional compromise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silenciosa controls, closers held
scenarios.trigger: If Silenciosa dictates an honest-but-not-scorching gallop and the prominent horses track her comfortably, setting up a straight-line battle for those who race prominently.
scenarios.body: Fallen Angel and Pacific Mission, both proven at the trip on Good ground, are ideally positioned to pounce from just off the pace as Silenciosa's effort flattens out in the closing stages; the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up from the rear in a race that never truly runs away.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate straight
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses surge past a fading Silenciosa early in the straight and the pace is just strong enough to stretch the hold-up contingent.
scenarios.body: Calendar Girl, stepping up in trip and unbeaten in three on Good ground, and Alobayyah, a winner here over course and distance, are ideally set to take over from Silenciosa and fight it out at the front; this scenario favours those who have already tracked a similar solo front-runner and quickened past it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses run on late
scenarios.trigger: If Silenciosa sets a stronger gallop than expected and the prominent pack over-commits, opening a clear late lane for closers.
scenarios.body: Noche Clasica, a dual course winner and strong finisher when the pace is genuine, and Mostar Dreams, with recent good-ground placed form, are the most likely beneficiaries of a collapse in the leading group; this shape is inherently unlikely given the single front-runner setting a comfortable tempo, but cannot be entirely dismissed if Silenciosa is pressured.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield chaos, scrambled finish
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types — Blingy's Sister, Rumba Numba, and Aviatrice — all attempt to reclaim their natural prominent position simultaneously, creating a congested, scrimmaging mid-race.
scenarios.body: A contested middle order disrupts the rhythm of every runner caught in traffic, and any beneficiary would be a horse lucky enough to find a clear run late; this shape is the least likely given the modest pace and the clear positional hierarchy that should form naturally behind Silenciosa.

watchPoints.text: Silenciosa's early pace is critical — if she dawdles before the straight, the entire field compresses and any horse with a tactical kick from prominence becomes extremely dangerous; watch her splits in the opening two furlongs.

Blingy's Sister, Rumba Numba, and Aviatrice are all natural prominent horses forced wide of their ideal position — if two or more of them attempt to push forward simultaneously in the early stages, expect scrimmaging between the 7f and 5f poles that could unsettle horses tracking behind.

Calendar Girl's 302-day absence is the most significant fitness unknown in the race; if Burrows has her cherry-ripe she is potentially the most dangerous prominent type given her unbeaten Good-ground record, but a return to full fitness after 10 months is not guaranteed.

Fallen Angel's hood (first-time headgear flag) is worth monitoring in the paddock — she arrives fresh at 86 days, and if she is edgy or fails to settle behind Silenciosa her prominent role could become a liability rather than an asset.

Maeva's 113-day absence combined with a sole poor performance on Good ground (1 from 8 runs on comparable conditions) suggests she is unlikely to be competitive unless the pace is stronger than anticipated — useful for context when assessing whether hold-up horses can realistically close.

races.name: Betway Ashton Heath Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Crimson Spirit
runners_data.note: Two wins over 7f on good ground in her last five runs is the standout stat here; Tom Marquand rides a hold-up type who needs the pace to be honest, and her 10-day turnaround with the Kublers in solid form (4 from 12 over 14 days) makes her a leading player if closers get their chance.
runners_data.comment: Crimson Spirit arrives in cracking nick — a winner last time out and second two starts back, with experience of today's trip and going. Carrying 142 lb from stall 4 is the weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Pellitory
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners a horse who has run 0 from 5 wins on good ground in recent starts, with finishing positions of 13th, 26th, and 16th in three of the last five suggesting she finds it harder to win on this surface than any other; hold-up style means she needs pace and a clear run that has often eluded her.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Pellitory nonetheless shaped with promise when second two runs back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 141 lb from stall one, our ratings mark him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Yanifer
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old prominent racer with proven course form — a win over 8f on good and a second over 7f in soft — who has gone rather flat in the last two runs (00); Harriet Bethell sends out just one runner in the past 14 days and Oisin McSweeney's local knowledge could help if the horse recaptures earlier-season form.
runners_data.comment: Yanifer showed smart form when winning four starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is that he's been unplaced in his last three outings heading into this.

runners_data.name: Wechaad
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old is the confirmed pace-setter and has won over this exact trip on soft going; his style fit flag reflects that he is stepping into a front-running role rather than his more natural prominent position, and the key question is whether he can sustain the gallop over 7f on good without being seriously pressured.

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse by design — headgear (blinkers) added to sharpen him — but with five horses preferring the rear the race shape has pushed him towards midfield in this map; Sean Levey's strongest recent form is at 8f on good, suggesting this trip is towards the minimum, and a win record of 1 from 15 on good ground adds further caution.
runners_data.comment: Third five starts back is the sole podium finish in his recent record, and Christian David arrives here fit on a 14-day turnaround, with experience over today's trip and going and a useful rating of 91 in his favour — the risk is that he's winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: New Image
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides a horse fitted with a visor who is, at heart, a deep closer best suited to races with a strong early gallop; with the map placing him in midfield against his natural instinct and two wins from 15 on good in his profile, this race shape is not an ideal fit even if the trainer's yard remains active.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts with unplaced efforts dominating recent form, New Image is hard to fancy despite a rating of 88 suggesting some ability; he has run over today's trip and going, and seven days since his last outing at least means fitness isn't a concern.

runners_data.name: Moonshine
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has won twice at 6f on standard and shows up well at shorter trips; 59 days off the track is the main query, but Kieran Shoemark rides a prominent type who gets a genuinely good draw to travel just behind Wechaad and could prove very dangerous if fitness is retained.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with a speed rating that lags the field, Moonshine is hard to fancy despite a lively recent profile — two wins in her last five starts — and a trainer firing at 28%; the 59-day absence adds another question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Wechaad is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger looking to press him hard from the off, he is set to control the tempo across Haydock's flat 7f on good ground — a setup that typically produces a fair, honest gallop rather than a searing pace. Moonshine and Yanifer will both look to track him prominently, so the lead group of three is likely to be closely bunched through the early and middle stages. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear in comfort: Christian David and New Image are genuine closers by nature but have been redistributed to midfield in this map given the volume of back-markers, meaning they may not secure their ideal late-running position. A controlled, single-pace gallop set by a lone leader favours horses that can travel just off the pace and sustain a challenge from two furlongs out — prominent-to-mid types who get a clean run will have the clearest chance, while true deep closers face a stern test if the tempo never truly injures the front group.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wechaad Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Wechaad is allowed to dictate an uncontested, sustainable tempo and the closers cannot generate enough momentum to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Wechaad bowls along untroubled at an honest but manageable gallop, and with nothing forcing his hand mid-race he conserves enough to repel late challengers entering the final furlong; horses that sit just behind him — Moonshine and Yanifer — are best placed to pounce if he does weaken, having tracked the pace throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Moonshine or Yanifer press Wechaad sufficiently through the middle of the race to expose him in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The increased mid-race tempo drains Wechaad's reserve, allowing one of the prominent stalkers to sweep past in the closing stages; Moonshine's recent wins at shorter suggest sharp acceleration while Yanifer's course experience at this trip on good ground is a meaningful asset.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Best
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to gut the front-runners and the hold-up horses find a clear passage in the straight.
scenarios.body: Crimson Spirit, whose two recent wins at 7f on good ground demonstrate she can finish powerfully when the race is truly run, would be the primary beneficiary; Pellitory also has the profile to close late but has struggled to win on good in recent starts, so needs everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Wechaad sets only a crawl and the race turns into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race compresses the field and removes any edge for hold-up types, turning the outcome into a battle of raw speed; Christian David and New Image, despite being true hold-up horses forced into a midfield position, would be at a significant disadvantage given their natural style does not suit a sprint-from-the-front scenario.

watchPoints.text: Wechaad's ability to maintain his lead beyond the two-furlong pole is the pivotal factor — if he ties up early, Moonshine and Crimson Spirit have the profiles to capitalise immediately.

Crimson Spirit and Pellitory are both genuine hold-up horses and may find themselves racing slightly too close to the pace if the field compresses behind Wechaad — watch for traffic issues rounding into the straight.

Moonshine's 59-day absence is a notable fitness flag; if Ed Walker has her cherry-ripe she is a serious danger, but if she needs the run she could weaken at exactly the point she would otherwise strike.

Christian David and New Image are both natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield in this pace map — should the pace be strong enough to create a true late-race scenario, they hold more theoretical ability than their current map positions suggest, but that shape requires conditions to work against their placement.

Yanifer's recent form reads 00 but both prior outings were over 7f on good — the same conditions today — so watch whether the prominent racer produces a market move suggesting connections expect a return to the 1-2 form of earlier in the season.

races.name: Betway Tanners Bridge Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Galba
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Kevin & Lauren Frost with a handy record on good ground (5/6 sim-going starts with three places); Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim is a useful weight relief, and 10 days since last run suggests freshness, though no win in seven similar-going starts is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Galba arrives here in fine fettle just 10 days since his last start, and his record of three placings in his last five runs underlines his consistency at this level; winless in recent starts, but he shapes as the one to beat stepping out from stall 8 carrying 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Liam Wright (5lb claimer) partners this consistent hold-up runner who has two wins from eleven starts on good ground and arrives on the back of consecutive wins; Charlie Clover's yard is at 1/6 over the past 14 days so form is modest but the horse's profile suits a truly-run 7f perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Norcross Brow arrives in fine nick — a winner last time out and a second the start before signals strong recent form, and he has experience of both today's trip and going. The main risk is the 136 lb burden from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Comprador
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Antony Brittain wearing a hood, returning from a 49-day break with no good-ground wins in six attempts on similar footing; likely to race prominently and ensure the pace is strong but the layoff and going record temper expectations considerably.
runners_data.comment: Comprador has placed third on four occasions in recent starts and shaped with promise throughout, while his experience over today's trip is a clear asset; the concern is that he's been winless in his last six outings and must bounce back from an unplaced effort 49 days ago.

runners_data.name: Black Endeavour
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Mark Rimell with a strong course-and-distance-relevant form line — two wins from nine on good — and tongue-tie fitted; Kieran Shoemark is a major upgrade in the saddle and 30 days since last run seems straightforward, though this is a step back up in trip from recent 6f efforts.
runners_data.comment: Black Endeavour won two starts back but has since finished sixth, and with a speed rating of 64 sitting below his official mark, he needs to find more on recent evidence; he has run over today's trip and going, and 30 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: One of three genuine front-runners, trained by David O'Meara and ridden by the in-form Daniel Tudhope; has a win over 8f on good ground and a solid record on similar going (7/8), but will face direct competition for the lead from Comprador and Horace Wallace which may cost him valuable energy early.
runners_data.comment: Napolian won three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, while 11 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; carrying 133 lb from stall 6 is the factor to weigh against his claims.

runners_data.name: Crafty Blue
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's charge has two wins but both came from a position at the front of the race — this horse is a natural hold-up or prominent type whose instinct is to race handy, and in a field this full of front-runners it is likely to be squeezed out of its ideal berth; Sean Levey knows the horse well but the pace map displacement is a genuine hazard.
runners_data.comment: Crafty Blue won last time out but that masks three finishes of ninth in her last five starts, and she ranks bottom of this field on our figures — a tough ask, though she does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Flyta
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell takes the ride on this hold-up type for Mark Loughnane who has a fine recent record — a win and three places from eight good-ground starts, tongue-tie fitted; consistent profile over trips around 7-8f on good, and the strong pace should set this horse up perfectly if it can find clear daylight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our assessments, Flyta faces a stiff task on these figures, yet she arrives in decent nick — a winner two starts back and second last time out — with experience over today's trip and going, and a light 11-day turnaround suggesting she's fit.

runners_data.name: Berlinetta
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Jack Channon who won last time out over 8f on good and has placed twice from seven similar-going starts; George Bass is a less established rider at this level but the horse's tactical profile suits a pace-honest race, and the step back to 7f from 8f should not inconvenience.
runners_data.comment: Berlinetta won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims, though that recent improvement follows back-to-back fifths and she carries 131 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Norfolk Blue
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a significant draw for William Knight's hold-up horse, which has shown consistent form placing at 7f and 8f on good ground; however this is a genuine rear-of-field type being mapped into midfield because the field is so full of hold-up horses — Murphy may navigate this well but the displaced position is a real challenge with a visor fitted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts despite a couple of runner-up finishes, Norfolk Blue ranks eighth of ten on our figures and his speed rating of 64 leaves plenty to find; he has run over today's trip and going before, and returns after just 15 days, but it's hard to get enthusiastic from stall five off 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Horace Wallace
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner for Richard & Fahey, returning from 49 days off with no good-ground wins from seven starts on similar going; Oisin McSweeney takes the ride but the combination of a long absence, weak recent form, and the likelihood of a gruelling battle for the lead with Napolian and Comprador makes this one to oppose rather than support.
runners_data.comment: Horace Wallace showed he can win, landing the spoils five starts back, but his last four have brought a fourth, an unplaced effort, a seventh and an eighth, and a trainer striking at just 2% recently is a concern despite experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian, Comprador, and Horace Wallace are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong, contested gallop from the outset over Haydock's flat 7f on good ground — there will be no tactical crawl here. These three will fight for early position and the resulting pace will be genuine, meaning every furlong will count and stamina reserves will be called upon in the final stages. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent horses who can sit off the hot pace and produce a sustained finish once the pace-setters begin to tire inside the final two furlongs. Crafty Blue and Norfolk Blue are true hold-up types who are pushed into the midfield section of the map because the field already carries more genuine rear-of-field runners than can realistically all secure that position; of the two, Crafty Blue's form suggests it can travel prominently enough, but neither should be expected to reproduce their best from a compromised berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out inside the first half-mile, leaving the field to be harvested by the hold-up horses tracking the pace.
scenarios.body: The contested lead from Napolian, Comprador and Horace Wallace creates a truly run race that sees them fade in the straight, giving horses coming from midfield or off the pace a decisive advantage in the final furlong. Norcross Brow and Flyta, both consistent hold-up types with good form on Good ground, are ideally positioned to reel in the tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-style runners tracks the leaders closely and pounces when the front-runners crack in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Black Endeavour and Berlinetta are both P-style horses who can sit just off the fast pace and deliver their challenge at the optimal moment when the leaders begin to tie up. Black Endeavour's course form over this sort of trip on good ground and Berlinetta's recent winning effort make both dangerous from this prominent slot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more evenly shared — with Horace Wallace or Comprador dropping away early — leaving one leader to control fractions and steal an unassailable advantage.
scenarios.body: Napolian, with Daniel Tudhope in the saddle and a win over further on good ground in recent form, is the best-credentialled of the three pace-setters to dictate on solo terms and last home if the pace settles. This scenario requires the other two front-runners to underperform or be outpaced early, a genuine possibility given Comprador's 49-day absence and Horace Wallace's patchy recent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively steady in the middle stages and none of the hold-up horses can generate a meaningful run from behind.
scenarios.body: With Crafty Blue and Norfolk Blue both displaced from their true hold-up roles and the other closers relying on everything going right positionally, an even gallop could leave the rear-of-field runners with too much ground to make up. In this scenario the prominent types who tucked in just behind the leaders — Black Endeavour, Berlinetta — collect the places while the closers finish flat.

watchPoints.text: Comprador and Horace Wallace — both return from 49-day breaks as confirmed front-runners; if either contests the lead vigorously with Napolian it could produce a suicidally fast early pace that benefits the hold-up horses dramatically.

Crafty Blue — Oisin Murphy's mount Norfolk Blue and Sean Levey's Crafty Blue are both genuine hold-up types squeezed into midfield; watch for traffic complications if these two converge around the 3f marker and block each other's runs.

Norcross Brow — has won twice recently and suits this race shape perfectly, but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/6 and a 5lb claimer in Liam Wright mean execution risk is real if the horse needs a well-timed delivery.

Black Endeavour — Kieran Shoemark's booking is eye-catching given the horse has only run once at 7f (sixth at Yarmouth on Standard), so watch whether it truly stays the trip when the strong pace asks questions in the last two furlongs.

Napolian — Daniel Tudhope is likely to attempt to dictate from the front, but with two rivals equally determined to lead, observe early whether he secures a clear rail position at the start; a wide draw or slow break could change the entire complexion of the race.

races.name: Betway Capital City Handicap Stakes (London Mile Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Cosi Bello
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent course-and-distance form (won over 7f on Good, placed repeatedly on Good ground), Tom Marquand booking is a positive, and 28 days between runs is straightforward — ideally drawn to sit just off the pace in a race that should play directly to her style.
runners_data.comment: Cosi Bello won three starts back and filled the runner-up spot five starts back, giving him recent winning form to build on; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating puts him narrowly top of this field — the risk is reproducing that level after two below-par efforts since.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose recent win came over 8f on Good but his wider handicap record shows poor strike-rate in similar conditions (1W1P from 15 Good-ground runs); 7 days since last run is quick and the apprentice claim of Seamus Cronin (5) may offset some of that concern.
runners_data.comment: Witch Hunter bounces back nicely after winning last time out, and he has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 142 lb from stall one, he arrives fresh on a seven-day turnaround, and our rating of 101 marks him as a lively each-way proposition despite a patchy recent record.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who is 0 from 15 on Good ground in handicap company — an alarming stat — and while he placed second last time, that was over 7f on Good and stepping up in company now; headgear note (t) adds a query, and Callum Rodriguez has a solid book.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying 139 lb from stall 7, Yorkshire has run over today's trip and going before and rates 8 lb above his official mark — making him a live danger. The risk is that he's been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Star Anthem
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 91 days off for Clive Cox, who sends out just 1 from 21 runners in 14 days — low volume stable — and has zero wins or places on Good ground in five attempts; the layoff is the biggest question mark.

Star Anthem has experience over today's trip and going, but he arrives winless in his last five starts, with only a third four starts back to show in recent form, and his trainer is in poor nick at 1/21 in the past fortnight — that 91-day absence adds another question mark.

runners_data.name: Mountain Cat
runners_data.note: Promising three-year-old trained by Saeed bin Suroor with two wins from three starts, both on Good or Standard, and drops slightly into handicap company for the first time; races prominently and the headgear change (p — first time?) warrants monitoring, but he arrives lightly raced and on an upward curve.
runners_data.comment: Mountain Cat won two starts back and again three starts back, but a seventh last time out clouds the picture after a 51-day break; he has run over today's trip and carries 136 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Skipper
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with two wins over this 8f trip on Good ground (including a Haydock win), though 75 days between runs is significant; headgear (b) retained and James Doyle's appointment is the standout jockey upgrade in this field.
runners_data.comment: Skipper won three starts back but has posted a sixth and ninth either side of that, and 75 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 136 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over 8f on Good last time out for Ed Walker, giving him strong going and trip credentials; Kieran Shoemark rides and 18 days is a routine gap — needs the pace to truly collapse ahead of him but is well positioned if it does.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him obvious claims, but four defeats before that latest success — including an eighth two starts back — suggest consistency remains a question mark at 135 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Tilted Kilt
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose only win came on Standard at 8f, and his Good-ground record (0W2P from 15 runs) is modest — Oisin Murphy takes over and the headgear change (p) is a first-time application to note; must hold out hope the pace shapes up perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Tilted Kilt has struggled badly in his last three starts, finishing eighth, unplaced, and seventh in recent outings, and ranks near the foot of the field on our figures; has run over today's trip and going, but little here suggests a revival.

runners_data.name: Leadman
runners_data.note: David O'Meara six-year-old with strong 7f Good-ground form (3W from 15 similar runs) but is a genuine hold-up type who is unlikely to secure his natural rear position in this pace-rich field — the style-fit discount is real and his chance is conditioned on whether he can settle mid-pack and produce his run anyway.
runners_data.comment: Leadman won three starts back but has disappointed since, finishing seventh last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall 14, and our rating of 90 suggests more than his official mark of 84 implies.

runners_data.name: Lost Signal
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Richard Hannon who is the benchmark pace figure in the race; a perfect 5-from-5 on Good ground and has won over a mile, so trip and conditions are not in question — the question is whether the duel with Inspired costs him his finish.
runners_data.comment: Lost Signal showed smart form when winning three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going keeps him firmly in the mix — the main concern is a 75-day absence heading into this competitive assignment.

runners_data.name: King Casper
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent handicap form shows a 17th and 13th in his last two starts — difficult to fancy on that evidence — and the wider record includes wins from much lower grades; Antony Brittain's 1-from-13 recent trainer strike rate does not help.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, King Casper at least has experience over today's trip and going, and 29 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; carrying 129 lb from stall 10, he looks up against it at a mark of 82 with nothing in recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: The other confirmed pace-setter, winning last time over this exact trip on Good for K.R. Burke, who is 7 from 43 in 14-day form — solid; drops in OR to 79 and carries 126lbs, giving her a weight advantage in a contested pace scenario, though if she and Lost Signal exhaust each other she will struggle to hold on.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Inspired faces a stiff ask against this field, and four finishes outside the placings in his last six starts underline the concern — though he does arrive on the back of a win and has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old boasts strong recent form (1W4P from 15 on Good ground) and has won over 10f, raising a query over whether the mile is ideal — a true hold-up runner who, because this field has an excess of hold-up types, is shown in midfield rather than his natural position, so his finishing kick may be blunted by the inability to fully switch off early.
runners_data.comment: Finished fourth last time out and ranks bottom of our figures among these 14 rivals, making him hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and experience over today's trip and going; the trainer's current 4% strike rate offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Triple Double A
runners_data.note: Prominent-gaited runner dropping back from 10-11f trips and returning to 8f for Hugo Palmer; headgear (tp) applied, three wins on Good at longer trips but his 8f record is less convincing — Harry Vigors (5) claims and the step back in trip is the defining query.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Triple Double A is hard to fancy despite a win six starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and 36 days' freshness offers some slim hope from stall 3.

races.paceDynamic: Lost Signal and Inspired are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this flat Haydock mile, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a soft gallop — both are proven front-runners on Good ground and neither will concede without a fight. With six of fourteen runners wanting prominent positions, the early exchanges will be congested and scrappy, compressing the midfield and generating legitimate pace pressure throughout, which should ensure an honest, rhythm-driven gallop rather than a dawdle that flatters closers. That pace profile gives prominent-tracking types — horses who can sit just off the front two and travel into the race without expending energy claiming position — the clearest structural advantage, as the lead duel between Lost Signal and Inspired is likely to blunt both of them late. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all be accommodated in role; Cosi Bello, Yorkshire, Mountain Cat, and Skipper have the best chance of actually locking into their natural position behind the two leaders, while Leadman and Financer — true hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map — are unlikely to secure their ideal pitch and should be discounted in any scenario that depends on an uncontested late run from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lost Signal and Inspired burn each other off at a genuine clip, leaving a prominent tracker to sprint clear.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners elevate the tempo and tie each other up in the final furlong, handing a decisive advantage to horses who tracked just behind them and arrive with energy intact; Cosi Bello, Mountain Cat, and Skipper are best positioned to pounce having raced within a length or two of the action without fighting for it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Inspired or Lost Signal establishes a clear lead without a sustained duel and dictates a controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: A solo pace-setter allows the leader to conserve energy through the middle section and produce a telling late kick; the horse that locks in smoothest early lead — most likely Inspired given her recent winning form — can repel the prominent trackers on that easier tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Times It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle becomes sufficiently attritional to drag the field into a ragged, strung-out contest where a well-placed midfield horse finds space two out.
scenarios.body: Arctic Thunder or Witch Hunter, hunting off the back of a genuine gallop, could deliver a well-timed run if gaps appear in a tiring field; both have the one-mile form on Good to capitalise, though they need the pace to fully stack up to bring their finishing kicks into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If a falsely run or fractured pace leaves a pocket of late energy at the back of the field to mow down a weakening front half.
scenarios.body: This scenario is markedly less likely given that Leadman and Financer — the horses who would typically execute a genuine hold-up finish — are pushed out of their natural rear position by the pace-heavy field and are unlikely to travel with the relaxation they need to produce their best; Star Anthem represents the outside chance here if the race completely misfires.

watchPoints.text: Watch the opening two furlongs closely as Lost Signal (stall position unknown) and Inspired clash for the lead — if neither gives ground the pace could turn race-shaping aggressive, dramatically improving prospects for Cosi Bello and Skipper sitting just behind.

Mountain Cat wears headgear for the first time (first-time p noted) and is a lightly raced three-year-old stepping into a 14-runner handicap for the first time — monitor how he settles behind a contested pace; if he races keenly he may not see out the mile.

Prominent congestion from runners 1-14 means Yorkshire, Skipper, and Cosi Bello may be scrubbing and jostling for position between 2-3 furlongs out as the field compresses — traffic danger is real and any horse trapped on the inside rail at that point is at risk of losing a length or more at the critical moment.

Leadman and Financer are genuine hold-up types who cannot get their ideal pitch in this field — if you see either horse making an uncharacteristic move for position in the first two furlongs, that is a sign they are racing against their instincts and their chance should be discounted further.

Skipper's 75-day absence is the form-fitness question of the race — watch his paddock and early demeanour; James Doyle's booking suggests connections believe he is fully wound up, but first run back after a long break over a flat mile is a real test.

races.name: Betway Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Suggy
runners_data.note: Trained by Charles Hills in strong recent form — two wins over 8f on Standard/AW — and Harry Vigors claims 5lb, but on Good turf at Haydock his sim-going record is 0W0P from two starts; a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to last all the way to the line.
runners_data.comment: Suggy has won two on the spin and arrives on a sharp eight-day turnaround, with experience over today's trip and going and an official mark of 79 giving him plenty to work with; the hefty 142 lb burden is the one factor to watch.

runners_data.name: Director's Cut
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over this C&D trip on Standard, and Connor Planas takes the ride for a trainer whose last-14-day record reads a poor 0/3; 40 days off the track is worth noting, but his role dictating from the front means freshness may not be a material concern.
runners_data.comment: Director's Cut won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat from stall one carrying 138 lb; the main concern is his unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Phantom Watch
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has the best sim-going profile of any runner here — 1W4P from ten starts on Good — making him the most reliable form reference for conditions; held up in the rear, Liam Wright will need to navigate traffic from a wide field but the form figures 23-412 suggest a consistent type who finds the line well.
runners_data.comment: Phantom Watch landed a win two starts back and was a close second last time out, showing he's in consistent form over today's trip and going. Carrying 138 lb from stall two, the 43-day break is the only question mark for the top-rated runner here.

runners_data.name: Home Hero
runners_data.note: A front-runner who ran just two days ago, which is an unusually short turnaround and raises a fitness/freshness query despite the win on his penultimate start over 8f Good; Hugo Palmer saddles both Home Hero and Phantom Watch, and Luke Catton rides, but the quick return combined with a modest sim-going record (1W2P) tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Home Hero won two starts back but comes here on a quick turnaround after finishing fifth just two days ago, and his inconsistent recent record — including a ninth three starts back — tempers enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 137 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed nine times from eleven starts on Good ground, including two wins and multiple seconds over 7-8f; Conor Whiteley claims 3lb and the horse has been in fine recent form — 255122 — suggesting he will press the front-runners naturally and be there at the finish.
runners_data.comment: Sandy Craic has shown real consistency, finishing second twice in her last two starts and landing a win three starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going — the main risk is whether she can convert her placed efforts into victory.

runners_data.name: Forever Endless
runners_data.note: Three career runs all ending in fifth place (form: 555), and while trained by Kevin & Lauren Frost with a 2/11 14-day strike rate, this horse is a genuine hold-up type that the field shape has pushed forward on the map — in reality it will likely trail the field and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 is warranted given the lack of any winning form.

runners_data.name: Sunshine And Roses
runners_data.note: Won last time over 8f on Standard, but the 12/8f Good run sits prominently in a mixed form profile; naturally a hold-up horse whose true racing style is unlikely to be expressed with this much pace in the race, and Rose Dawes rides at an OR of 60 — the lowest-rated runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win last time out but has otherwise been inconsistent in recent starts, finishing fourth twice and unplaced once before that; she has run over today's distance and going, yet ranked sixth of seven on our figures, she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Golden Mabel
runners_data.note: Tagged for fading in the finish and has never won in six career starts (form: 857868), with the visor headgear not having unlocked improvement; Matthew Slater claims 5lb but this hold-up type will be navigating traffic from the rear and the weight of evidence suggests she is likely to be involved only in the minor placings at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent outings, Golden Mabel faces a stiff ask ranked bottom of the field on our figures; the experience over today's trip and going, plus a quick turnaround, are slim consolations.

races.paceDynamic: Director's Cut and Home Hero are the two confirmed front-runners and will battle for early supremacy from the gates, ensuring this mile is run at a genuine, honest gallop rather than a falsely-run tactical crawl. With two genuine pace horses pressing each other through Haydock's flat mile on Good ground, the tempo is unlikely to relent, which typically sets up a contest for those who can travel smoothly in behind and quicken off a true pace. Sandy Craic, with a prominent style, is well-placed to sit just off the pace and exploit any weakening of the leaders late, while Phantom Watch and Suggy — true hold-up horses — will need the pace to last long enough to deliver late runs. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; Forever Endless, Sunshine And Roses, and Golden Mabel are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in this field shape with two front-runners dominating the early sections, Director's Cut and Home Hero are overwhelmingly likely to secure the positions that matter up front, with Sandy Craic the most natural beneficiary of the prominent slot behind them. This race shape — a contested, genuine-paced mile — strongly favours prominent horses who can track the pace and produce a sustained late effort over closers who rely on a dawdle to close ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Director's Cut and Home Hero fight for the lead and set a genuine gallop that stretches the field from early, leaving prominent trackers to pounce.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up through the early and middle sections, and a horse sitting just off the pace in a prominent position is ideally placed to pick them off in the final two furlongs; Good ground at Haydock rewards a sustained gallop and penalises those who close too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Smoothly
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Director's Cut — establishes a clear lead early and Home Hero fails to match strides, allowing solo control of the tempo.
scenarios.body: With a solo leader setting a controlled but genuine pace, the race becomes a test of which horse sustains rhythm to the line rather than who quickens sharpest; a front-runner able to dictate without being pressed can ghost clear before closers fully organise their runs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough throughout to set up a race where hold-up horses, having stayed off early trouble, produce the strongest finish in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Suggy has the best recent form of the true hold-up types — two wins from eight starts on Soft/Standard — and would be the principal beneficiary if the tempo remains strong all the way to the two-furlong pole; Phantom Watch, with four placings and one win in similar conditions, also fits this shape but needs the race to be truly run end-to-end.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Closers Flattered
scenarios.trigger: If Home Hero fails to press Director's Cut and the early fractions ease into a falsely-run gallop, compressing the field and flattening out the pace advantage.
scenarios.body: A bunched, falsely-run mile on Good ground can produce a sprint finish that theoretically aids hold-up horses, but with Forever Endless, Sunshine And Roses, and Golden Mabel all racing out of their natural role and carrying STYLE_FIT discounts, none represent reliable beneficiaries in this shape; Sandy Craic's proven turn of foot at the trip remains the most transferable asset even in this compressed scenario.

watchPoints.text: Director's Cut and Home Hero will lock horns for the early lead — watch how aggressively Home Hero jumps and whether the two-day turnaround shows in his early energy, as a contested duel between them could set a frantic pace that burns out both front-runners by the two-furlong pole.

Sandy Craic's draw and Conor Whiteley's positioning from the gate is critical — if he gets shuffled back behind the mid-pack rather than tracking the pace naturally in third or fourth, he loses the advantage his prominent style confers on a genuine-paced mile.

Phantom Watch's visor and hold-up style means Liam Wright will need a clear run in the last two furlongs; with three redistributed hold-up horses also looking to close from similar positions, traffic congestion in the straight is a genuine risk for those finishing from deep.

Forever Endless, Sunshine And Roses, and Golden Mabel are all true hold-up horses that the pace map has redistributed to midfield — watch whether any of them actually break away from the rear and take a more prominent position than their natural style suggests, which would change the race shape materially.

Home Hero's two-day turnaround warrants watching in the paddock and at the start — Hugo Palmer runs both Home Hero and Phantom Watch, and any signs of dullness or reluctance from Home Hero in the early stages could hand Director's Cut an uncontested lead and transform the race dynamic entirely.
